truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 identified many supplied vulnerabilities but missed five items, misclassified or overclaimed several severities and CWE mappings, and included extra findings not present in the supplied truth set.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string vulnerability in debug logging
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the unsafe printf call using runtime_log_format and explained that the format can be controlled through configuration.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer overflow and undefined behavior in factorial function
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the factorial result *= i overflow path, although it underclaimed the severity.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Memory pool cleanup frees memory while thread pool tasks may still use it
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified stage_deferred_history_flush, memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup, the sleeping worker task, and scratch pool memory being used after cleanup.
The previous answer identified the command constructed from validator_cmd and config_file and the system() call in the admin validate path.

The previous answer reported the unsafe strcpy into input_buffer_ and also separately reported the safe_string_copy off-by-one involving dest[src_len] and src_len > dest_size, together covering the supplied anchors.
The previous answer identified the read-before-lock pattern old_value = value_, lock_guard, and value_ = old_value + 1 as a data race.

The previous answer found the login_attempts_ > 5 and EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE authentication logic, but classified it as an authentication bypass with CWE-287 and Critical severity rather than the supplied logic bomb CWE-511 High item.
The previous answer identified config_dir_ + filename in load_config and the admin load path that can bypass the intended config directory.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into fixed 256-byte parser buffer
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified buffer_size_ = 256, allocation of expression_buffer_, and unbounded strcpy into that pool-backed buffer during expression parsing.
The previous answer identified the hardcoded ADMIN_SECRET value SC_ENT_2025_AUTH.
The previous answer identified the weak 1000 to 9999 session token range but did not explicitly identify the non-cryptographic std::mt19937 PRNG used to generate it.
No previous finding discussed the static cached_time in log_debug_message or the thread-unsafe localtime caching.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection in emergency audit logging
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the environment-controlled supercalc_emergency.log path and system() call, but framed the issue primarily as command injection rather than the supplied insecure temporary file handling item.
No previous finding identified persistent authenticated_, session_token_, and login_attempts_ state as a CWE-613 persistent authentication state issue.
No previous finding identified the unhandled std::stod exception risk in handle_variable_command.
No previous finding identified the size_t underflow risk in the memory pool block split calculation using SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded recursion in parser for nested parentheses
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified parse_factor recursively calling parse_expression on PAREN_OPEN without enforcing the configured recursion limit.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race in expression result cache
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified result_cache_ being read and written in evaluate_cached without using cache_mutex_ while tasks may run from the thread pool.
No previous finding identified the TOCTOU window between std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and opening the config file.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) and the zero token_length case.
